nom: The Ordinary UV Filters SPF 45 Serum

segments.oily: Reviewers with oily skin are split: several report the formula is light, glowy, and non-greasy once it settles, while others explicitly warn it is too heavy or greasy for oily skin, and one reviewer with oily skin reports her skin burned and broke out badly.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin are mixed: several appreciate the glow and hydration, calling it ideal for dry skin, while others report it feels heavy or greasy on application, and a couple report bumps or a reaction.
segments.combination: Most reviewers with combination skin report good results, including no breakouts and a moisturizing effect; one reviewer with combination, fair, somewhat sensitive skin, however, reports irritation and breakouts appearing after a few days.
segments.sensitive: Reviewers with sensitive skin are sharply divided. A large group reports serious reactions - red bumps, rashes, hives, swelling, or burning, in some cases severe enough to need medical treatment - often surfacing two or three days into use. A separate group of sensitive-skin reviewers, however, reports no reaction at all, even after weeks of daily use.
segments.mature: The one reviewer who mentions mature skin alongside acne-proneness reports a healthy glow and no ashy cast.
segments.normal: Several reviewers who describe their skin as normal, with no history of reacting to skincare, report serious reactions to this sunscreen specifically - itchy bumps, redness, or breakouts across the face and neck - despite never having had a problem with other products.

concerns.redness: A large cluster of reviewers, including some who describe their skin as normal or only mildly sensitive, report serious reactions: red, itchy bumps, rashes, hives, swelling, or burning, in some cases severe enough to need medical treatment or steroids, often surfacing two or three days into use rather than immediately. A separate, smaller group of reviewers with sensitive skin, however, report zero reaction even after weeks of daily use. Several reviewers also specifically report the sunscreen stinging or burning their eyes.
concerns.blemishes: Many reviewers with acne-prone skin report no breakouts and even clearer skin with regular use. A substantial minority, however, report the opposite: new breakouts, closed comedones, or clogged-pore bumps, in some cases appearing only after several days of use and taking about a week to resolve; a few reviewers specifically warn acne-prone users to avoid it.
concerns.oiliness: Reviewers are divided on how it wears through the day: many report it absorbs into a non-greasy, glowy finish, while others, including several with oily skin, report it stays visibly oily, shiny, or greasy, especially right after application.
concerns.dehydration: A few reviewers describe the sunscreen as hydrating, including one who sought it out specifically as her skin became more prone to dehydration; one reviewer, however, reports it left her skin patchy, dry, and itchy alongside a burning reaction.

aspects.libelle: Looks greasy at first, absorbs into a glow
Leaves no white cast for most
Can sting or burn eyes, especially when sweating
Layers well under makeup without pilling

extraits.titre: 1 Star – Would Give Zero If I Could
extraits.texte: Please be careful with this sunscreen. I don't even consider my skin super sensitive, but The Ordinary's new sunscreen gave me one of the worst allergic reactions I've ever had. Within hours, I broke out in painful hives all over my face. Antihistamines didn't help—I've been on steroids for a week now and still have a rash that won't go away. I bought this hoping it would be a good alternative to my favorite sunscreen from Natrium, but it was a huge mistake. I truly wish I had never tried it. If you have even mildly reactive skin, I strongly recommend avoiding this product. I wouldn't wish this experience on anyone.

Please believe all of the users who said that this is very sensitive for people with sensitive skin. The first day that I used this went really great. I am an African-American female with normal skin. I don't usually have any kind of reactions to products, and I have many products from this line, but after about three days of daily use, I noticed red, small bumps that were all over the skin where I used the sunscreen. Please believe the other users, this broke me out all over my lower jaw and neck, as well as in the corners of my eyes. I returned it expeditiously and I will never use this product again. I wish I could give it zero stars.

I couldn't believe how fast my skin went downhill using this product. For context I have a normal skin type, sometimes tending towards dry, and have never experienced a reaction to a skincare product. This SPF gets 1 extra star because I liked the consistency and it settled well without leaving a white cast on me (though I am very fair.) Everything else has been awful in my personal experience. Day one was perfectly fine, but by the end of day two using this sunscreen every inch of my skin was covered in small, itchy under the skin bumps. I can tell it was this product because even my neck and hands where I applied the excess are broken out. Such a waste and an unbelievable experience from The Ordinary considering how highly regarded they are by myself and many others.

I tried this sunscreen cause I liked the price-point and enjoy all The Ordinary products I have tried, when I tell you this is the worst sunscreen I have ever put in my face... believe me. My skin burned and broke out so horribly and is still recovering after a week. I have oily skin but I would describe my sensitivity as normal. I genuinely am so disappointed in this product, and advise anyone, ever to read all these reviews and stay away.

This sunscreen is great! The serum texture is a nice alternative to thick versions. It does appear greasy at first, but after it dries down, it leaves the most beautiful glow. It layers well under makeup. I have sensitive skin and have had no reaction after using for 3 weeks. Highly recommend!

I know some people were complaining about greasy heavy feel on certain skin types. I have oily skin at baseline and I felt like this sunscreen is so light weight/elegant on the skin. I'm in my 30s and feel like my skin is more prone to dehydration lately. So applying this feels more like a hydrating hug. I don't feel it on my skin throughout the day. Spreads easily like a dream despite using typical American filters. Glow is stunning and enhances my makeup bases. I think they did an excellent job formulating this sunscreen and it is my new favorite daily go to.

I know all skin is different but this works great for my skin. I'm prone to breakouts and have combination skin. This worked well as both a sunscreen and very effective moisturizer for me. I don't wear make-up so not sure how make-up would build on top of this. It goes on VERY greasy but then blends in and I never felt oily. I'm on my second bottle.
